key_insight: A temporal machine learning time-to-event model combined with ALSFRS-R trajectories can personalize predictions of ALS functional decline and wheelchair-free survival.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help clinicians anticipate assistive device needs earlier and support care planning, trial stratification, and precision medicine.
method: Harmonized longitudinal ALS records with diagnosis, ALSFRS-R, activities of daily living, and demographics.
Used clustering and generalized additive mixed models to map domain-specific decline across bulbar, upper limb, axial, lower limb, and respiratory function.
Built a temporal ML + Cox time-to-event framework to generate individualized survival curves and predict wheelchair access timing.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a harmonized longitudinal cohort and modeling pipeline with domain-level and survival analyses, but does not provide performance metrics in the summary.
watch_item: External validation and real-world integration are needed to confirm generalizability, calibration, and safe use across diverse ALS populations.
paper_title: A Temporal Machine Learning-Based Time-to-Event Model for Predicting ALS Progression and Healthcare Utilization
